claim: A genetically engineered mouse model, termed Klf1K74R/K74R or Klf1(K74R), carrying mutation on the well-conserved sumoylation site of the hematopoietic transcription factor KLF1/EKLF has been generated that possesses extended lifespan and healthy characteristics, including cancer resistance.
source: A genetically engineered mouse model, termed Klf1K74R/K74R or Klf1(K74R), carrying mutation on the well-conserved sumoylation site of the hematopoietic transcription factor KLF1/EKLF has been generated that possesses extended lifespan and healthy characteristics, including cancer resistance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the mouse model generated in previous work.

claim: The healthy longevity characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice, as exemplified by their higher anti-cancer capability, are likely gender-, age-, and genetic background-independent.
source: We show that the healthy longevity characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice, as exemplified by their higher anti-cancer capability, are likely gender-, age-, and genetic background-independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1 showing anti-cancer capability across different genders, ages, and genetic backgrounds.

claim: The anti-cancer capability, in particular that against melanoma as well as hepatocellular carcinoma, and lifespan-extending property of Klf1(K74R) mice, could be transferred to wild-type mice via transplantation of their bone marrow mononuclear cells at a young age of the latter.
source: Significantly, the anti-cancer capability, in particular that against melanoma as well as hepatocellular carcinoma, and lifespan-extending property of Klf1(K74R) mice, could be transferred to wild-type mice via transplantation of their bone marrow mononuclear cells at a young age of the latter.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 showing transfer of anti-cancer capability via BMT.

claim: NK(K74R) cells carry higher in vitro cancer cell-killing ability than wild-type NK cells.
source: Furthermore, NK(K74R) cells carry higher in vitro cancer cell-killing ability than wild-type NK cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 demonstrating higher cytotoxicity of NK(K74R) cells.

claim: Targeted/global gene expression profiling analysis has identified changes in the expression of specific proteins, including the immune checkpoint factors PDCD and CD274, in the leukocytes of the Klf1(K74R).
source: Targeted/global gene expression profiling analysis has identified changes in the expression of specific proteins, including the immune checkpoint factors PDCD and CD274, and cellular pathways in the leukocytes of the Klf1(K74R) that are in the directions of anti-cancer and/or anti-aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry data in Figure 4 showing differential expression of PDCD and CD274.

claim: Changes in cellular pathways in the leukocytes of the Klf1(K74R) are in the directions of anti-cancer and/or anti-aging.
source: Targeted/global gene expression profiling analysis has identified changes in the expression of specific proteins, including the immune checkpoint factors PDCD and CD274, and cellular pathways in the leukocytes of the Klf1(K74R) that are in the directions of anti-cancer and/or anti-aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomics analysis and pathway enrichment data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Aging of animals, including humans, is accompanied by lifespan-dependent organ deterioration and the occurrence of chronic diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular failure, and neurodegeneration.
source: Aging of animals, including humans, is accompanied by lifespan-dependent organ deterioration and the occurrence of chronic diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular failure, and neurodegeneration (Aman et al., 2021; López-Otín et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Multiple blood cell lineages arise from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), with the lymphoid lineage giving rise to T, B, and natural killer (NK) cell populations, whereas the myeloid lineage differentiates into megakaryocytes, erythrocytes, granulocytes, monocytes, and macrophages.
source: Multiple blood cell lineages arise from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), with the lymphoid lineage giving rise to T, B, and natural killer (NK) cell populations, whereas the myeloid lineage differentiates into megakaryocytes, erythrocytes, granulocytes, monocytes, and macrophages (Mitchell et al., 2022; Pálovics et al., 2022; Seita and Weissman, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing hematopoietic lineages.

claim: EKLF, also named KLF1, is a Krüppel-like factor that is expressed in a range of blood cells, including erythrocytes, megakaryocytes, T cells, NK cells, as well as in various hematopoietic progenitors.
source: EKLF, also named KLF1, is a Krüppel-like factor that is expressed in a range of blood cells, including erythrocytes, megakaryocytes, T cells, NK cells, as well as in various hematopoietic progenitors, including common myeloid progenitor , megakaryocyte erythroid progenitor (MEP), and granulocyte macrophage progenitor (Frontelo et al., 2007; Nishizawa et al., 2016; Teruya et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing KLF1 expression patterns.

claim: KLF1 regulates erythropoiesis.
source: The factor regulates erythropoiesis (Perkins et al., 2016) and the differentiation of MEP to megakaryocytes and erythrocytes (Frontelo et al., 2007; Neuwirtova et al., 2013) as well as of monocytes to macrophages (Luo et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: KLF1 regulates the differentiation of MEP to megakaryocytes and erythrocytes.
source: The factor regulates erythropoiesis (Perkins et al., 2016) and the differentiation of MEP to megakaryocytes and erythrocytes (Frontelo et al., 2007; Neuwirtova et al., 2013) as well as of monocytes to macrophages (Luo et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: KLF1 regulates the differentiation of monocytes to macrophages.
source: The factor regulates erythropoiesis (Perkins et al., 2016) and the differentiation of MEP to megakaryocytes and erythrocytes (Frontelo et al., 2007; Neuwirtova et al., 2013) as well as of monocytes to macrophages (Luo et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: KLF1 is expressed in HSC and regulates their differentiation.
source: KLF1 is also expressed in HSC and regulates their differentiation (Hung et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: KLF1 could be sumoylated in vitro and in vivo.
source: KLF1 could be sumoylated in vitro and in vivo, and sumoylation of the lysine at codon 74 of mouse KLF1 altered the transcriptional regulatory function (Frontelo et al., 2007) as well as nuclear import (Shyu et al., 2014) of the factor.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Sumoylation of the lysine at codon 74 of mouse KLF1 altered the transcriptional regulatory function of the factor.
source: KLF1 could be sumoylated in vitro and in vivo, and sumoylation of the lysine at codon 74 of mouse KLF1 altered the transcriptional regulatory function (Frontelo et al., 2007) as well as nuclear import (Shyu et al., 2014) of the factor.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Sumoylation of the lysine at codon 74 of mouse KLF1 altered nuclear import of the factor.
source: KLF1 could be sumoylated in vitro and in vivo, and sumoylation of the lysine at codon 74 of mouse KLF1 altered the transcriptional regulatory function (Frontelo et al., 2007) as well as nuclear import (Shyu et al., 2014) of the factor.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Homozygosity of a single amino acid substitution, lysine(K) to arginine(R), at the sumoylation site of KLF1 results in the generation of a novel mouse model with healthy longevity.
source: Surprisingly, homozygosity of a single amino acid substitution, lysine(K) to arginine(R), at the sumoylation site of KLF1 results in the generation of a novel mouse model with healthy longevity.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work described in the manuscript.

claim: Klf1(K74R) mice exhibited extended healthspan and lifespan.
source: These mice, termed Klf1K74R/K74R or Klf1(K74R), exhibited extended healthspan and lifespan.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work and data in the manuscript.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice showed delay of the age-dependent decline of physical performance, such as the motor function and spatial learning/memory capability.
source: In particular, the Klf1(K74R) mice showed delay of the age-dependent decline of physical performance, such as the motor function and spatial learning/memory capability, and deterioration of the structure/function of tissues, including the heart, liver, and kidney.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice showed delay of deterioration of the structure/function of tissues, including the heart, liver, and kidney.
source: In particular, the Klf1(K74R) mice showed delay of the age-dependent decline of physical performance, such as the motor function and spatial learning/memory capability, and deterioration of the structure/function of tissues, including the heart, liver, and kidney.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice appeared to have significantly higher anti-cancer capability than the WT mice.
source: Furthermore, the Klf1(K74R) mice appeared to have significantly higher anti-cancer capability than the WT mice (Shyu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and data in the current manuscript.

claim: Male as well as female Klf1(K74R) mice in the B6 genetic background had significantly fewer pulmonary melanoma foci than the corresponding WT mice.
source: It appeared that male as well as female Klf1(K74R) mice in the B6 genetic background had significantly fewer pulmonary melanoma foci than the corresponding WT mice (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Both young (2-month-old) and aged (24-month-old) Klf1(K74R) mice had higher anti-metastasis ability against the injected melanoma cells than WT mice of age-dependent groups.
source: First, both young (2-month-old) and aged (24-month-old) Klf1(K74R) mice had higher anti-metastasis ability against the injected melanoma cells than WT mice of age-dependent groups (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Homozygosity of the K74R substitution was required for the higher cancer resistance of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: Secondly, homozygosity of the K74R substitution was required for the higher cancer resistance of the Klf1(K74R) mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice in the FVB background exhibited a high cancer resistance than FVB WT mice.
source: Importantly, the Klf1(K74R) mice in the FVB background also exhibited a high cancer resistance than FVB WT mice by this assay (Figure 1C), suggesting that cancer resistance of Klf1(K74R) mice conferred by the homozygous K74R substitution was likely genetic background-independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cancer resistance of Klf1(K74R) mice conferred by the homozygous K74R substitution was likely genetic background-independent.
source: Importantly, the Klf1(K74R) mice in the FVB background also exhibited a high cancer resistance than FVB WT mice by this assay (Figure 1C), suggesting that cancer resistance of Klf1(K74R) mice conferred by the homozygous K74R substitution was likely genetic background-independent.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that cancer resistance is observed in both B6 and FVB genetic backgrounds.

claim: The higher anti-cancer capability of the Klf1(K74R) mice did not appear to depend on the arginine at codon 74.
source: Finally, the higher anti-cancer capability of the Klf1(K74R) mice did not appear to depend on the arginine at codon 74 since Klf1(K74A) mice carrying K→A amino acid substitution at the K74 sumoylation site also exhibited higher anti-metastasis capability than WT mice in the pulmonary foci assay (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D comparing K74A mice to WT mice.

claim: Klf1(K74A) mice carrying K→A amino acid substitution at the K74 sumoylation site exhibited higher anti-metastasis capability than WT mice in the pulmonary foci assay.
source: Finally, the higher anti-cancer capability of the Klf1(K74R) mice did not appear to depend on the arginine at codon 74 since Klf1(K74A) mice carrying K→A amino acid substitution at the K74 sumoylation site also exhibited higher anti-metastasis capability than WT mice in the pulmonary foci assay (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Klf1(K74R) mice carry a higher anti-cancer capability against hepatocellular carcinoma than the WT mice.
source: As shown by the subcutaneous inoculation assay of Hepa1-6 cells (Figure 1E), Klf1(K74R) mice also carry a higher anti-cancer capability against hepatocellular carcinoma than the WT mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice are resistant to the carcinogenesis of a range of different cancers.
source: It thus appears that the Klf1(K74R) mice are resistant to the carcinogenesis of a range of different cancers.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that Klf1(K74R) mice show resistance to both melanoma and hepatocellular carcinoma.

claim: Blood replacement of recipient mice with 10 Gy γ-irradiation by that of the donor mice reached 90% in the seventh week.
source: Blood replacement of recipient mice with 10 Gy γ-irradiation by that of the donor mice reached 90% in the seventh week (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: WT mice transplanted with WT BMMNC had similarly high numbers of tumor foci relative to WT mice without BMT.
source: We found that WT mice transplanted with WT BMMNC had similarly high numbers of tumor foci relative to WT mice without BMT (Figures 1A and 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing WT→WT BMT to control mice.

claim: WT mice that received BMMNC from Klf1(K74R) mice presented significantly fewer tumor foci on their lungs.
source: However, similar to Klf1(K74R) mice challenged with B16-F10 cells (Figure 1B), WT mice that received BMMNC from Klf1(K74R) mice presented significantly fewer tumor foci on their lungs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: BMT using 24-month-old donor mice gave similar results, although the effect is relatively small.
source: Notably, BMT using 24-month-old donor mice gave similar results, although the effect is relatively small (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BMT using two lower doses of γ-irradiation (2.5 Gy/5 Gy) still resulted in the transfer of cancer resistance from Klf1(K74R) to WT mice.
source: BMT using two lower doses of γ-irradiation (2.5 Gy/5 Gy) still resulted in the transfer of cancer resistance from Klf1(K74R) to WT mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Approximately 40% of recipient blood cells were substituted by donor cells upon BMT with 5 Gy γ-irradiation.
source: Approximately 40% of recipient blood cells were substituted by donor cells upon BMT with 5 Gy γ-irradiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At 5 Gy irradiation dosage, BMT from Klf1(K74R) mouse donors reduced the average number of pulmonary tumor foci in recipient WT mice to 5.
source: Consequently, at that irradiation dosage, BMT from Klf1(K74R) mouse donors reduced the average number of pulmonary tumor foci in recipient WT mice to 5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Only 20% blood replacement was achieved in the recipient mice with 2.5 Gy γ-irradiation.
source: On the other hand, only 20% blood replacement was achieved in the recipient mice with 2.5 Gy γ-irradiation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The WT mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice developed less number (~10/mouse) of pulmonary tumor foci than those WT mice receiving BMT from the WT mice at 2.5 Gy irradiation.
source: However, the WT mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice again developed less number (~10/mouse) of pulmonary tumor foci than those WT mice receiving BMT from the WT mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Even at a low level of 20% blood replacement, BMT still enabled effective transfer of cancer resistance from Klf1(K74R) mice to WT mice.
source: Thus, even at a low level of 20% blood replacement, BMT still enabled effective transfer of cancer resistance from Klf1(K74R) mice to WT mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that 20% blood replacement still resulted in reduced tumor foci.

claim: The median lifespan of WT mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice was 5 mo longer than that of WT mice receiving BMT from WT mice.
source: Significantly, the median lifespan of WT mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice was 5 mo longer than that of WT mice receiving BMT from WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The longer lifespan characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice were transferable via BMT.
source: Thus, the longer lifespan characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice were also transferable via BMT.
evidence: This claim is supported by the lifespan data from BMT experiments.

claim: Klf1(K74R) bone marrow carried the anti-metastasis capability that prevented melanoma cell colonization in the lungs of recipient mice.
source: Our experiments indicated that Klf1(K74R) bone marrow carried the anti-metastasis capability that prevented melanoma cell colonization in the lungs of recipient mice (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Tumor growth in mice subjected to BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice was significantly slower relative to those receiving BMMNC from WT mice.
source: As shown, tumor growth in mice subjected to BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice was significantly slower relative to those receiving BMMNC from WT mice (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Klf1(K74R) BMMNC can inhibit the growth of tumors more effectively than WT BMMNC.
source: Thus, Klf1(K74R) BMMNC indeed can inhibit the growth of tumors more effectively than WT BMMNC.
evidence: This claim is supported by the tumor growth inhibition data from Figure 3.

claim: The population of NK(K74R) cells in 24-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice was higher than the WTNK cells in 24-month-old WT mice.
source: In general, the cell populations in peripheral blood (PB) were not affected much by the K74R substitution, as shown by CBC analysis (Shyu et al., 2022), although flow cytometry analysis of PB from WT and Klf1(K74R) mice of different ages showed that the population of NK(K74R) cells in 24-month-old Klf1 (K74R) mice was higher than the WTNK cells in 24-month-old WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The K74R substitution did not alter the expression levels of KLF1 protein in leukocytes from PB.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, the K74R substitution did not alter the expression levels of KLF1 protein in leukocytes from PB (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, left panels), although the Klf1 mRNA level of Klf1 (K74R) leukocytes was 10–20% lower than that of WT leukocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Klf1 mRNA level of Klf1(K74R) leukocytes was 10–20% lower than that of WT leukocytes.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, the K74R substitution did not alter the expression levels of KLF1 protein in leukocytes from PB (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, left panels), although the Klf1 mRNA level of Klf1 (K74R) leukocytes was 10–20% lower than that of WT leukocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Klf1 gene is expressed in B220+ B cells, CD3+ T cells, and NK cells of both WT and Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: By western blotting (WB) analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B) and RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), we found that the Klf1 gene is expressed in B220+ B cells, CD3+ T cells, and NK cells of both WT and Klf1(K74R) mice, but the levels are much lower than that of the erythroid MEL cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: The mRNA levels of Pdcd and Cd274 in the PB, B cells, and T cells of WT mice were both increased during aging.
source: As shown in Figure 4, the mRNA levels of Pdcd and Cd274 in the PB, B cells, and T cells of WT mice were both increased during aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mRNA levels and protein levels of Pdcd and Cd274 were lower in 3-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice than the age-matched WT mice.
source: In contrast, the mRNA levels and protein levels of these two genes were lower in 3-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice than the age-matched WT mice, and they remained low during aging of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mRNA levels and protein levels of Pdcd and Cd274 remained low during aging of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: In contrast, the mRNA levels and protein levels of these two genes were lower in 3-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice than the age-matched WT mice, and they remained low during aging of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4.

claim: RNAi knockdown of Klf1 expression reduced Pdcd and Cd274 mRNA levels in splenic CD3+ T cells.
source: Significantly, RNAi knockdown of Klf1 expression reduced Pdcd and Cd274 mRNA levels in splenic CD3+ T cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Overexpression of KLF1 would increase the expression of Cd274 in mouse CD4+ T cells.
source: In an interesting correlation, overexpression of KLF1 would increase the expression of Cd274 in mouse CD4+ T cells (Teruya et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: KLF1 positively regulates the transcription of the Pdcd and Cd274 genes, directly or indirectly.
source: These data together indicate that KLF1 positively regulates the transcription of the Pdcd and Cd274 genes, directly or indirectly, and likely the transcriptomes of a diverse range of hematopoietic cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNAi knockdown and overexpression data.

claim: Change of the expression of Pdcd and Cd274 genes was most likely caused by the loss of the sumoylation of KLF1(K74R), which would alter its transactivation capability.
source: Since the levels of KLF1 protein in CD3+ T (K74R) cells and WT CD3+ T cells were similar (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B), change of the expression of Pdcd and Cd274 genes (Figure 4) was most likely caused by the loss of the sumoylation of KLF1(K74R), which would alter its transactivation capability (Siatecka and Bieker, 2011).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that KLF1 protein levels are similar but gene expression differs, combined with citation to literature on sumoylation effects.

claim: Pdcd appeared to be a direct regulatory target of KLF1.
source: Interestingly, Pdcd appeared to be a direct regulatory target of KLF1.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: KLF1 was bound at the CACCC box (Box3) at –103 of the Pdcd promoter in CD3+ T cells from both WT and Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: As shown by ChIP-qPCR analysis, KLF1 was bound at the CACCC box (Box3) at –103 of the Pdcd promoter in CD3+ T cells from both WT and Klf1(K74R) mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Lower levels of Pdcd and Pdcd1 expression were observed in the PB of mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: As expected, lower levels of Pdcd and Pdcd1 expression were also observed in the PB of mice receiving BMT from Klf1(K74R) mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The low tumorigenesis rate of Klf1(K74R) mice arises in part from the low expression of the two ICGs, Pdcd and Cd274, as a result of K74R substitution in the KLF1 protein.
source: These findings together suggest that the low tumorigenesis rate of Klf1(K74R) mice arises in part from the low expression of the two ICGs, Pdcd and Cd274, as a result of K74R substitution in the KLF1 protein.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations of low ICG expression and low tumorigenesis.

claim: There was no significant difference in the serum levels of IL-1β, IL-2, IL-10, IL-12p70, INF-γ, or TNF-α between WT and Klf1(K74R) mice at 24-month-old.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4, there was no significant difference in the serum levels of IL-1β, IL-2, IL-10, IL-12p70, INF-γ, or TNF-α between WT and Klf1(K74R) mice at 24-month-old.
evidence: This claim is supported by bead-based multiplex assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The level of IL-4 in 24-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice was three- to fourfold higher than the 24-month-old WT mice.
source: In contrast, the level of IL-4, an anti-inflammatory cytokine (Ul-Haq et al., 2016) beneficial to the hippocampus of aging mice (Boccardi et al., 2018), in 24-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice was three- to fourfold higher than the 24-month-old WT mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by bead-based multiplex assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The level of IL-6 increased only moderately during aging of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: On the other hand, the level of IL-6, a key factor in chronic inflammatory diseases, autoimmunity, cytokine storm, and cancer (Menees et al., 2021; Rea et al., 2018), increased only moderately during aging of the Klf1(K74R) mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by bead-based multiplex assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The altered expression of some of the cytokines in the blood likely contributes to the anti-aging and/or anti-cancer characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: Thus, similar to PDCD and CD274, the altered expression of some of the cytokines in the blood likely also contributes to the anti-aging and/or anti-cancer characteristics of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observed differences in cytokine expression patterns.

claim: A total of 259 and 306 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified between the two age groups for the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice, respectively.
source: A total of 259 and 306 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified between the two age groups for the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomics analysis data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The age-dependent DEPs changed in the concordant direction in the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice were enriched for several known aging-related pathways, for example, IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, DNA repair, etc.
source: To understand the correlations of these proteins with aging and cancer, we performed the Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) and found that the age-dependent DEPs changed in the concordant direction in the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice were enriched for several known aging-related pathways, for example, IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, DNA repair, etc. (Fabian et al., 2021; Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The age-dependent DEPs changed in the reverse directions in the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice were enriched for nine other aging-related pathways.
source: Meanwhile, the age-dependent DEPs changed in the reverse directions in the WT and Klf1(K74R) mice were enriched for nine other aging-related pathways (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Only 7 DEPs were identified in the 3-month-old mice but 40 DEPs in the 24-month-old ones.
source: As shown in Figure 5D, only 7 DEPs were identified in the 3-month-old mice but 40 DEPs in the 24-month-old ones.
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomics analysis data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Of the 40 DEPs in the elder mice, 3 and 37 were upregulated in Klf1(K74R) and WT mice, respectively.
source: Of the 40 DEPs in the elder mice, 3 and 37 were upregulated in Klf1(K74R) and WT mice, respectively (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomics analysis data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were enriched for the anti-aging pathways related to hypoxia, p53 signaling, etc.
source: Significantly, GSEA of these DEPs showed that elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were enriched for the anti-aging pathways related to hypoxia, p53 signaling, etc. (Yeo, 2019; Zhu et al., 2021), while the elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the aging-associated pathways related to apoptosis, mTORC1 signaling, etc (Yeo, 2019; Hamarsheh et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the aging-associated pathways related to apoptosis, mTORC1 signaling, etc.
source: Significantly, GSEA of these DEPs showed that elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were enriched for the anti-aging pathways related to hypoxia, p53 signaling, etc. (Yeo, 2019; Zhu et al., 2021), while the elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the aging-associated pathways related to apoptosis, mTORC1 signaling, etc (Yeo, 2019; Hamarsheh et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The DEPs in elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were enriched for anti-cancer pathways related to the IFN-α response, TGF-β signaling, etc.
source: On the other hand, the DEPs in elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were also enriched for anti-cancer pathways related to the IFN-α response, TGF-β signaling, etc. (Ni and Lu, 2018; Principe et al., 2014; Zitvogel et al., 2015; Figure 5E), while DEPs in the elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the pro-cancer pathways related to IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling and angiogenesis (Zhao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: DEPs in the elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the pro-cancer pathways related to IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling and angiogenesis.
source: On the other hand, the DEPs in elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes were also enriched for anti-cancer pathways related to the IFN-α response, TGF-β signaling, etc. (Ni and Lu, 2018; Principe et al., 2014; Zitvogel et al., 2015; Figure 5E), while DEPs in the elder WT leukocytes were enriched for the pro-cancer pathways related to IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling and angiogenesis (Zhao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Klf1(K74R) leukocytes contribute to their anti-cancer capability and long lifespan through several specific cellular signaling pathways.
source: These data together have demonstrated that Klf1(K74R) leukocytes contribute to their anti-cancer capability and long lifespan through several specific cellular signaling pathways.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the pathway enrichment analysis data.

claim: NK(K74R) cells exhibited significantly higher cytotoxicity against the B16-F10 melanoma cells than WT NK cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6, NK(K74R) cells exhibited significantly higher cytotoxicity against the B16-F10 melanoma cells as well as Hepa1-6 hepatocellular carcinoma cells than WT NK cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by Calcein-AM cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: NK(K74R) cells exhibited significantly higher cytotoxicity against Hepa1-6 hepatocellular carcinoma cells than WT NK cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6, NK(K74R) cells exhibited significantly higher cytotoxicity against the B16-F10 melanoma cells as well as Hepa1-6 hepatocellular carcinoma cells than WT NK cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by Calcein-AM cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: NK cells play an important role in the higher anti-cancer capability of the hematopoietic blood system of Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: This data, together with the higher level of NK cells in aged Klf1(K74R) mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), indicated that in parallel to the leukocytes (Shyu et al., 2022), NK cells also play an important role in the higher anti-cancer capability of the hematopoietic blood system of Klf1(K74R) mice, as exemplified in Figures 2 and 3.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations of higher NK cell cytotoxicity and higher NK cell levels in aged mice.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice are ideal as an animal model for further insightful understanding of the aging process as well as for biomedical development of new anti-aging tools and approaches.
source: With respect to the above, the Klf1(K74R) mice (Shyu et al., 2022) are ideal as an animal model for further insightful understanding of the aging process as well as for biomedical development of new anti-aging tools and approaches.
evidence: This claim is a speculative statement about the potential utility of the mouse model.

claim: The anti-cancer capability of the Klf1(K74R) mice is not due to the structural and/or post-translational properties of the arginine introduced at codon 74 of KLF1.
source: The anti-metastasis property of the Klf1(K74A) mice in the pulmonary foci assay (Figure 1D) also indicates that the anti-cancer capability of the Klf1(K74R) mice is not due to the structural and/or post-translational properties of the arginine introduced at codon 74 of KLF1.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that K74A mice also show anti-cancer capability.

claim: Homozygosity of K74R substitution causes one or more types of the hematopoietic cells to gain new functions, such as the higher cancer cell-killing capability of NK(K74R) cells.
source: It is likely that homozygosity, but not heterozygosity, of K74R substitution causes one or more types of the hematopoietic cells to gain new functions, such as the higher cancer cell-killing capability of NK(K74R) cells (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that homozygosity is required for cancer resistance and NK cells show higher cytotoxicity.

claim: The amount of specific types of cells such as NK(K74R) in the 20% of blood cells carrying homozygous Klf1(K74R) alleles in the recipient mice upon BMT is sufficient to confer the mice a higher anti-cancer ability.
source: The data of Figure 2D further suggest that the amount of specific types of cells such as NK(K74R) in the 20% of blood cells carrying homozygous Klf1(K74R) alleles in the recipient mice upon BMT is sufficient to confer the mice a higher anti-cancer ability.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that 20% blood replacement is sufficient for anti-cancer effect.

claim: Certain characteristics of the young mice could be transferred to old mice via heterochronic parabiosis or heterochronic transplantation.
source: Also, certain characteristics of the young mice could be transferred to old mice via heterochronic parabiosis or heterochronic transplantation (Conboy et al., 2005; Das et al., 2019; Goodell and Rando, 2015; Kang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Plasma proteins from human umbilical cord blood can revitalize hippocampal function and neuroplasticity in aged mice.
source: Similarly, plasma proteins from human umbilical cord blood can revitalize hippocampal function and neuroplasticity in aged mice (Castellano et al., 2017; Mehdipour et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Multiple injections of LSK-HSC(K74R) from 3-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice to 25-month-old WT mice would extend the lifespan of the latter by about 4 months.
source: Previously, we have shown that multiple injections of LSK-HSC(K74R) from 3-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice to 25-month-old WT mice would extend the lifespan of the latter by about 4 months (Shyu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: 2-month-old WT mice receiving one-time transplantation of BMMNCs from 2-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice would live 5.5 mo longer than the controls.
source: In the current study, we further show that 2-month-old WT mice receiving one-time transplantation of BMMNCs from 2-month-old Klf1(K74R) mice would live 5.5 mo longer than the controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Transplantation/transfer of the blood MNC carrying homozygous mutation at the sumoylation site of KLF1 could be developed as a new approach for long-term anti-aging, anti-cancer, and likely rejuvenation.
source: Thus, transplantation/transfer of the blood MNC carrying homozygous mutation at the sumoylation site of KLF1 could be developed as a new approach for long-term anti-aging, anti-cancer, and likely rejuvenation.
evidence: This claim is a speculative statement about potential applications of the findings.

claim: The tumorigenesis resistance and long lifespan exhibited by the Klf1(K74R) mice are most likely due to changes in the transcription regulatory properties of the mutant KLF1(K74R) protein relative to WT.
source: The tumorigenesis resistance and long lifespan exhibited by the Klf1(K74R) mice are most likely due to changes in the transcription regulatory properties of the mutant KLF1(K74R) protein relative to WT (Siatecka et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations and supported by citation to literature on KLF1 function.

claim: Cancer incidence increases with aging.
source: Notably, cancer incidence increases with aging (Aunan et al., 2017), which is accompanied by increased expression of PDCD and CD274 (Lages et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Aging is accompanied by increased expression of PDCD and CD274.
source: Notably, cancer incidence increases with aging (Aunan et al., 2017), which is accompanied by increased expression of PDCD and CD274 (Lages et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The lower expression of ICGs would contribute to the anti-cancer capabilities of the Klf1(K74R) blood to fight against cancer and to extension of the lifespan of cancer-bearing mice.
source: The lower expression of ICGs would contribute to the anti-cancer capabilities of the Klf1(K74R) blood to fight against cancer (Figures 1—3) and to extension of the lifespan of cancer-bearing mice (Shyu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations of lower ICG expression and higher anti-cancer capability.

claim: Changes in the pathways in the elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes relative to the elder WT leukocytes are mostly in the direction of anti-aging.
source: As summarized by the model in Figure 5F, it appears that changes in these pathways in the elder Klf1(K74R) leukocytes relative to the elder WT leukocytes are mostly in the direction of anti-aging.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The KLF1(K74R) amino acid substitution causes a change in the global gene expression profile of the leukocytes, which contributes to the high anti-cancer capability and long lifespan of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
source: The data of Figure 5 together strongly suggest that the KLF1(K74R) amino acid substitution causes a change in the global gene expression profile of the leukocytes, which contributes to the high anti-cancer capability and long lifespan of the Klf1(K74R) mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the proteomics and pathway analysis data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The transferability of the cancer resistance and extended lifespan of the mutant mice via transplantation of BMMNC suggests the possibility of future development of hematopoietic blood cells genome-edited at the conserved sumoylation site of KLF1 for anti-cancer and the extension of healthspan and/or lifespan in animals including humans.
source: Finally, the transferability of the cancer resistance and extended lifespan of the mutant mice via transplantation of BMMNC suggests the possibility of future development of hematopoietic blood cells genome-edited at the conserved sumoylation site of KLF1 for anti-cancer and the extension of healthspan and/or lifespan in animals including humans.
evidence: This claim is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mice had a spontaneous cancer incidence of 12.5% in life.
source: The Klf1(K74R) mice appeared to be cancer resistant to carcinogenesis as manifested by their lower spontaneous cancer incidence (12.5%) in life than WT mice (75%).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: WT mice had a spontaneous cancer incidence of 75% in life.
source: The Klf1(K74R) mice appeared to be cancer resistant to carcinogenesis as manifested by their lower spontaneous cancer incidence (12.5%) in life than WT mice (75%).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: The Klf1(K74R) mutation protected the mice from metastasis of melanoma cells and reduced melanoma growth in the subcutaneous cancer cell inoculation assay.
source: The Klf1(K74R) mutation also protected the mice from metastasis of melanoma cells and reduced melanoma growth in the subcutaneous cancer cell inoculation assay (Shyu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: B16-F10 cells are poorly immunogenic and highly aggressive.
source: The cultured melanoma B16-F10 cells used in this assay are poorly immunogenic and highly aggressive, thus being useful for monitoring early metastasis in various immunotherapy studies (Vaseghi et al., 2023; Díaz-García et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing B16-F10 cell characteristics.

claim: NK cells are effector lymphocytes of the innate immune system that can rapidly destroy tumor cells and against infectious pathogens.
source: NK cells are effector lymphocytes of the innate immune system that can rapidly destroy tumor cells and against infectious pathogens (Roncagalli et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: NK cells do not require pre-stimulation for the treatment of cancer cells.
source: Also, NK cells do not require pre-stimulation for the treatment of cancer cells (Yu, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The NK lineage could be fully reconstituted 2 wk after BMT.
source: Furthermore, the NK lineage could be fully reconstituted 2 wk after BMT (Ferreira et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.
